angle: Stop making users learn your AI stack—give them one front door, task-first.
sourceTitle: Google’s Gemini has a branding problem, and so does the rest of AI
linkedinPost:
If your users need a decoder ring to pick the right AI, you’ve already lost adoption.

TechCrunch’s take on AI branding nails a real enterprise problem: we make people learn product architecture instead of getting work done. Model names, tiers, modes—none of that maps to a task under deadline.

In the field, our highest-adoption launches have one front door and task-first labels. Not “Model X Ultra,” but “Refund an Order.” Not “Vision Pro,” but “Flag Damage.” Behind the door, we can route to the right engine. The user should never have to care.

My playbook: a service catalog of AI-powered actions with stable URLs/buttons, a single chat/command surface, and guardrails that auto-select the cheapest engine that meets the SLA. Change the plumbing as much as you want—never the surface.

If your AI feels like a product line, it will be evaluated like one—and many won’t bother.

Where could you replace five AI entry points with one “Do My Task” button? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
